title: Dhangadhi Service Bus: tracing an application across roles
summary: A proposed risk-based test plan for municipal approvals, document checks, payment states, and notifications.

sections.title: My development contribution
paragraphs: The CV documents my work on e-KYC, migration, recommendations, appointments, workflow routing, payments, document management, and notifications using Next.js, NestJS, GraphQL, and PostgreSQL.

sections.title: Risk & proposed scope
paragraphs: The highest-impact risks in this exercise are unauthorized decisions, applications stranded between officers, and inconsistent payment or document states. The proposed scope follows an application from submission to a terminal decision, including return and resubmission paths.

sections.title: Example test scenarios
items: Unauthorized approval: use a citizen account; expect rejection with no state change.
Send back and resubmit: preserve application history and show the latest submitted documents.
Stale action: two officers act from the same starting state; prevent conflicting terminal decisions.
Payment pending: refresh and retry; reconcile against the agreed payment state without duplication.
Notification routing: notify the intended recipient with the correct application reference.

sections.title: Evidence & release criteria
paragraphs: Capture starting role, application ID, state, request, and resulting audit trail for each scenario. Proposed release criteria require resolved high-impact authorization and data-integrity failures, with blocked integrations explicitly listed.
Status: design only. These scenarios have not been executed as part of this portfolio, and no defect counts or improvement metrics are asserted.

title: Vibe College: a test strategy for configurable enrollment
summary: A proposed study of conditional fields, saved drafts, intake rules, review transitions, and offer-letter consistency.

sections.title: My development contribution
paragraphs: My CV records a drag-and-drop form builder, configurable intakes, course selection, application workflows, offer letters, and installment management. The stack includes Next.js, Node.js, REST APIs, and PostgreSQL.

sections.title: Risk & fixture design
paragraphs: Use synthetic applicants and at least two form versions. Clarify whether existing drafts remain tied to their original version or migrate. Define required fields, file limits, course availability, and allowed reviewer transitions before setting expected results.

sections.title: Example test scenarios
items: Required value omitted: reject submission with a useful field message.
A conditional field becomes hidden: verify how its old value is handled.
Draft reopens after intake changes: apply the agreed version policy without silent data loss.
Repeated submit: avoid duplicate accepted applications.
Approved application: generate the offer from the correct course, applicant, and fee configuration.

sections.title: Evidence & proposed outcome
paragraphs: Compare UI input, request payload, saved record, reviewer view, and generated document. Record the schema version alongside the application identifier.
The proposed output is a traceable regression checklist with documented configuration dependencies. Status: design only; execution results are not available.

title: Syanko POS: protecting order and payment consistency
summary: A proposed regression study for order submission, kitchen tickets, billing arithmetic, payment ambiguity, and printing.

sections.title: My development contribution
paragraphs: My CV lists development of order management, kitchen order tickets, automated bills, taxes, discounts, multiple payment methods, and thermal receipts using React, Node.js, REST APIs, and PostgreSQL.

sections.title: Risk & proposed scope
paragraphs: The proposed focus is a mismatch between what the cashier sees, what the kitchen receives, and what the customer pays. Confirm rounding, discount ordering, cancellation, and retry rules before execution. Use a payment sandbox and synthetic orders.

sections.title: Example test scenarios
items: Submit twice during a slow response: inspect accepted order count and kitchen tickets.
Apply a discount at its agreed limit: compare the total with an independent calculation.
Delayed payment response: maintain an explicit pending state and reconcile the result.
Receipt printer fails: reprint the receipt without recharging.
Amend an already dispatched order: verify the agreed kitchen update and bill adjustment.

sections.title: Evidence & release criteria
paragraphs: Link the order ID, payment reference, kitchen ticket, and receipt. Keep expected calculations separate from application code. Proposed release criteria require no unresolved duplicate-charge or order-loss failures in the executed scope.
Status: design only. No live payment tests, measured improvements, or production defect claims are included.
